note: Admission is a claim made at a point in time against a stated standard, not a permanent property. This is a developmental evaluation: the criteria change as lessons are learned, so what passed D1 at widget 20 may fail the D1 of widget 51. Treating admission as permanent is what left three implementations of one operation, nine example-bound widgets and four port names encoding a use in a registry whose every member had passed its own review honestly. The widget audit's own Method section is where the permanence came from: D3 and D4 were sampled because 'doing it retroactively for all of them is a separate task', and D5, D6, D8 and D9 were declared 'not applicable retroactively'. That separate task was never scheduled. So each criterion now records when it last CHANGED and when the set was last SWEPT against it. A criterion changed after its last sweep is a re-admission debt: validate:admission fails, and the only ways to clear it are to sweep or to record why the change does not reach the existing set.

criteria.asks: Does each qualifier live on the input rather than in each consumer?
criteria.note:
Swept 2026-10-12, and the sweep refuted the reason it had never been swept. The audit called D5 not applicable retroactively because it governs design; the contestability note said whether a qualifier sits on the input or in each consumer is a structural property of built code. The note was right: it took one pass.

82 parameters are bare strings; most are labels, titles and notes, which are free text by design. Eight are genuine qualifiers.

FAILS -- free text checked only for non-emptiness, with no enumeration anywhere: rate.numeratorPeriod, rate.denominatorVintage, slr_threshold_comparison.verticalDatum. The first two even carry messages explaining why they matter ('a rate joins two things measured at different times') while checking nothing but that something was typed.

WEAK PASS: slr_extract_import.baselinePeriod, validated by the pattern /\d{4}/.

PASSES AT THE CONSUMER, NOT THE INPUT: table_input.unit is unvalidated where it is declared, and slr_extract_import refuses any unit it cannot interpret, naming metre or millimetre. That is the project's recorded stance -- declaring a unit does not verify it -- but only that one consumer enumerates, so another consumer of a table could accept anything.

DECLARATION WITH NO CONSEQUENCE: sample_raster.valueUnit is recorded as stated or unstated and never interpreted or scaled by.

BEST CASE, and the one D5 actually describes: slr_threshold_comparison's scenario, basis, family, year and quantile take their values from the key columns of the connected projection table, so the enumeration lives on the input exactly as the criterion asks.

But that best case carries a silent failure found while sweeping it. A selection matching NO ROW returns null, which flows on as unknown and is indistinguishable from genuinely missing data. The comment says 'A missing value stays unknown; it is never scaled into a number', which is right for a missing value and wrong for a missing row: no row means the selection matched nothing, which is a configuration error, not a data gap. This is the distinction experiment 65 names for unmatched subjects, one layer down -- an unmatched subject is a gap in the ruleset, not a finding about the data.

criteria.asks: Does the evidence test the distinction, not only the arithmetic?
criteria.note:
Swept partially 2026-10-12, and the sweep's own result is why it had never been swept: the obvious mechanisation under-detects exactly the cases the criterion is about.

THE PORT-BASED PASS. 15 live widgets declare two or more inputs of distinct carrier kinds. Two of those are presentation -- map_output and table_output -- where D8 does not apply. Of the remaining 13, seven carry lab parity, and five of those seven join two genuinely real sources: the John Snow checks (voronoi, clip_polygons, summarize_polygons, reachable_nodes, reachable_corridor, snap_to_network) take published 1854 point data and a real OSM street network, so a case exists using real data from both. Those pass. Six computing joiners have no independent case at all and fail by default: access, coverage_check, facilities, isochrone, sample_raster, slr_site_assignment.

WHY THAT IS NOT A SWEEP. The two widgets D8 most clearly applies to are invisible to it. slr_threshold_comparison declares ONE input port, assignments:table, and joins a projected sea-level change from the AR6 dataset with a supplied elevation from facility records on an unchecked datum -- it is the audit's own worked example of a D8 failure. rate declares ONE input port, records:points, and its whole purpose is joining a numerator and a denominator measured at different times from different sources; numeratorPeriod and denominatorVintage exist because the sources differ.

So a join is a property of the COMPUTATION, not of the port signature, and D8 as written -- 'any computation joining two independently sourced quantities' -- gives the audit procedure no way to enumerate its own subjects. Completing D8 means reading each widget's computation rather than its contract. That is recorded as a stated limit rather than left as a silent gap, and it is a finding about the criterion as much as about the widgets.

criteria.question: Does a residual function remain that no existing entity performs?
criteria.note:
Added 2026-10-12, from the practitioner's framing: what is the impact on workflows if this entity is absent, and can other entities take over its function? It is D1 for vocabulary, and it is sharper than asking for prior art, because a reference can always be found for something adjacent and adjacency is how a reinvention gets justified. A function either has a performer in this graph or it does not.

Applied: fw:Carrier FAILS -- removing it left SHACL conforming, 361 unit and 97 browser tests passing, and one grep hit, the paragraph explaining its absence. Four of the five functions it claimed were already performed by prov:Entity, prov:wasGeneratedBy, prov:used and fw:workflowNode, with 18, 26 and 22 assertions in a single run; the fifth, structure, is performed by geo:FeatureCollection, fw:PointDataset and fw:DataTable and is under-asserted at 3 assertions across 12 node outputs -- a gap independent of the class.

fw:PortType PASSES on the same test: no standard names the declared type of a workflow port, thirteen instances exist, and two ports connect when and only when these are equal.

setChanged.note: TWO changes in one day. coverage_check retired into clip_points_to_area, closing D2 on the practitioner's decision: a widget that REPORTED a membership and a widget that ACTED on one were the same question asked twice. And deduplicate_points added, which D2 should be asked about directly -- it is near compare_point_sets, which pairs two layers BY ARRAY POSITION for geoprivacy and is not a record matcher, and near measure_distance, whose nearest-neighbour search it reuses rather than repeats. That reading was done when the widget was built and is recorded in its release; it has not been swept as a criterion here. D1, D7 and D10 were last swept against a set that no longer exists.
